mechanism_narrative: Accelerating residential concentration (RESIDENTIAL rising from 13.7% to 18.7% over four weeks) indicates sustained lockdown conditions that suppress all out-of-home mobility. RETAIL_REC will continue declining over the next four weeks as the residential shift deepens.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL increased 5.0 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the mean over the last 28 days, or RESIDENTIAL fails to increase further in the first two weeks ahead.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has collapsed to -59.6% at t-0w, indicating public transport avoidance. This barrier to retail access persists over the next four weeks, preventing recovery of RETAIL_REC even if restrictions ease, because commuting infrastructure remains underutilized.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -55% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at t-0w is -59.6%, lowest in series
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers above -40% within two weeks and RETAIL_REC subsequently rises above its t-0w level by week 4.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has declined monotonically from -36.6% to -46.1% over four weeks, signaling sustained remote work adoption. This erosion of commuting routines reduces incidental retail visits during work-week transit, suppressing RETAIL_REC recovery over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 5 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES declined 9.5 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rebounds above -40% within two weeks and RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility remains stable at -14% to -17%, indicating essential-goods shopping is resilient and substitutes for discretionary retail. As RESIDENTIAL concentration increases, consumers optimize trips to combine essential and discretionary purchases. RETAIL_REC recovery depends on whether GROCERY_PHARM stabilization signals confidence to broaden shopping scope.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM variance falls below 2 percentage points over two weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM range is only 2.4 percentage points across four weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM drops below -20% or RESIDENTIAL stops increasing, and RETAIL_REC fails to rise above -50% by week 2.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has oscillated between -12.0% and -1.6%, showing volatile outdoor activity patterns. When PARKS mobility rises above -5%, it signals consumer confidence in outdoor socializing, which typically precedes indoor retail recovery by one to two weeks as behavioral norms shift.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -5% for one week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at t-1w was -1.6%, highest in series
failure_condition: PARKS remains below -10% for the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC declines further despite PARKS recovery.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are both severely depressed (-59.6% and -46.1% respectively at t-0w), indicating coordinated restrictions on mobility infrastructure and workplace access. This dual constraint will persist over the next four weeks, preventing RETAIL_REC recovery unless policy explicitly reopens retail independently of transit and workplace restrictions.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain below -45% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both declined monotonically over four weeks
failure_condition: Either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES recovers above -35% within two weeks, and RETAIL_REC subsequently rises above -50% by week 4.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has accelerated its decline from -40.9% to -63.0% over four weeks, a 22.1 percentage point drop. This trajectory indicates a regime shift toward deeper lockdown. Absent a policy reversal signal visible in TRANSIT or WORKPLACES recovery, the momentum of RETAIL_REC decline will continue over the next one to two weeks before stabilizing.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC declines more than 10 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell 14.9 percentage points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -55% in week 1 ahead, contradicting the momentum-based decline hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL concentration has increased 5.0 percentage points while RETAIL_REC has fallen 22.1 percentage points over four weeks, indicating a strong substitution effect: consumers are shifting from out-of-home retail to home-based consumption. This substitution will persist over the next four weeks if RESIDENTIAL continues rising, keeping RETAIL_REC suppressed.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises more than 2 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL and RETAIL_REC moved in opposite directions across all four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL declines below 17% or RETAIL_REC rises above -50% despite continued RESIDENTIAL increase, indicating substitution effect has reversed.
